Flight Software Engineer (Early Career)
Golden, CO
Apply

Today, everything we send to space is constrained by what fits inside a rocket fairing. That's a fundamental bottleneck to building more capable spacecraft. Rendezvous Robotics is solving this problem with electromagnetic self-assembling tiles: modular spacecraft components that rendezvous, dock, and latch to assemble bigger and more powerful spacecraft than anything that can be folded to fit into a rocket.

We're a small team based in Golden, Colorado, executing on a clear path from flight demonstration to our first operational systems. Our work spans hardware, software, and systems engineering. We are looking for the best people in the world who want to build the next generation of advanced spacecraft.

This is an early career role for software and computer engineers. If you're graduating in 2027, you'd start in summer 2027. If you're already working and have two years or less of relevant experience, you're just as welcome, and you could start sooner. We care about what you've built and how you approach a hard problem. You probably haven't worked on a spacecraft yet, and that's fine. We'll teach you how to design for space. We're looking for people who have built real things and who keep asking questions until they understand why something works.

Responsibilities & Ownership

    Getting up to speed on writing software for space (fault tolerance, radiation upsets, updating a vehicle that's already in orbit)
    Flight software in C++ and C, from device drivers and firmware up through the components that wire subsystems together
    The embedded Linux on our flight computers: building images, debugging on target, and keeping the services on it healthy
    Microcontroller firmware for the sensors and actuators that move and dock our vehicles
    Tests, CI, and hardware-in-the-loop setups that catch problems before they reach a vehicle
    Bringing new boards into the software stack alongside the avionics team

Basic Qualifications

    BS or MS in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field, completed by summer 2027
    Two years or less of relevant professional experience (internships and co-ops don't count toward this)
    Real programming ability in C or C++, from coursework, research, or projects
    You've written software that talks to physical hardware, like a microcontroller, a sensor, a motor, or a robot
    Comfort working in Linux from the command line, with git
    A working understanding of what happens underneath your code: memory, pointers, and how a program actually runs on a processor

Preferred Qualifications

    Leadership in an engineering student organization such as Formula SAE, a rocketry club, a CubeSat or satellite team, a robotics team, or Solar Car, especially if you owned the software or electronics for a vehicle and saw it through to competition or flight
    An internship or co-op in embedded, aerospace, robotics, or automotive software
    Microcontroller firmware (STM32, ESP32, or similar), on an RTOS or bare metal
    Serial buses (UART, SPI, I2C) and bringing up a new device from its datasheet
    Python for test and tooling, plus CMake and CI
    Flight software or robotics frameworks such as F Prime or ROS

Compensation and Benefits

Engineer (Early Career): $85,000 - $115,000

Your actual base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. In addition to the base salary, you may also be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options. You will receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, short- and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and paid parental leave. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year.

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Equal Opportunity

Rendezvous Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Rendezvous Robotics is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

As a government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA), we request this information in order to measure the effectiveness of the outreach and positive recruitment efforts we undertake pursuant to VEVRAA. Classification of protected categories is as follows:

A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: a veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs; or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service-connected disability.

A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three-year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.

An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.

An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.
